No graph item and everyday scenarios: rule conflicts reported, not resolved. No ∑F = ma: Matt removed the acceleration problem (not before 3.4).

sectionsContent.title: Frictionless Inclines

items: Weight is Fg = mg, with g = 9.8 m/s² (S3.1). A free-body diagram has one labelled arrow per force (S3.2).
Split a force with sin and cos (S2.1). On a ramp, tilt your axes along and perpendicular to the ramp (S3.3).

sectionsContent.directions: Draw a free-body diagram for each problem, then answer in your notebook. Every ramp is frictionless. Give each force a unit and a direction, like down the ramp.

questions.prompt: Ty sets his 3.20 kg skateboard on a smooth ramp tilted 20.0° above the horizontal and lets go. Find the skateboard's weight, the part of that weight pulling it down the ramp, and the part pressing it into the ramp.
questions.solution: Fg = mg = 3.20 × 9.8 = 31.4 N down. Fg,parallel = 31.36 sin 20.0° = 10.7 N down the ramp. Fg,perp = 31.36 cos 20.0° = 29.5 N into the ramp.
questions.finalAnswer: Fg = 31.4 N down; Fg,parallel = 10.7 N down the ramp; Fg,perp = 29.5 N into the ramp

row: F_{g,parallel} = mg sin θ = (31.36 N) sin 20.0°
F_{g,perp} = mg cos θ = (31.36 N) cos 20.0°

steps.say: Only two forces act: F_{g} and F_{N}. The parallel and perpendicular parts are pieces of F_{g}, not extra arrows.

questions.prompt: An 18.0 kg box of books sits on the rollers of a loading ramp tilted 35.0° above the horizontal. The rollers make the ramp frictionless. Find the force pulling the box down the ramp and the normal force on the box.
questions.solution: Fg = 18.0 × 9.8 = 176.4 N. Fg,parallel = 176.4 sin 35.0° = 101 N down the ramp. FN = mg cos θ = 176.4 cos 35.0° = 144 N, perpendicular to the ramp, away from its surface.
questions.finalAnswer: Fg,parallel = 101 N down the ramp; FN = 144 N perpendicular to the ramp

row: F_{N} = mg cos θ = (176.4 N) cos 35.0°

steps.say: F_{N} = mg cos θ only because nothing else pushes into or pulls away from the ramp.

questions.prompt: Mia props up a board with books to make a ramp for her brother's 0.250 kg toy car. First the board is tilted 15.0° above the horizontal. Then she adds books until it is tilted 50.0°.
parts: a.  At each angle, find the force pulling the car down the ramp and the normal force on it.
b.  Which force grows as the ramp gets steeper, and which one shrinks?
questions.solution:
Fg = 0.250 × 9.8 = 2.45 N.
a. 15.0°: Fg,parallel = 2.45 sin 15.0° = 0.634 N down the ramp; FN = 2.45 cos 15.0° = 2.37 N perpendicular to the ramp. 50.0°: Fg,parallel = 2.45 sin 50.0° = 1.88 N down the ramp; FN = 2.45 cos 50.0° = 1.57 N perpendicular to the ramp.
b. The pull down the ramp grows (sin θ grows); the normal force shrinks (cos θ shrinks).
questions.finalAnswer: 15.0°: 0.634 N down the ramp, FN 2.37 N. 50.0°: 1.88 N down the ramp, FN 1.57 N. The down-ramp pull grows; FN shrinks.

row: 15.0°:  F_{g,parallel} = (2.45 N) sin 15.0° = 0.634 N down the ramp
50.0°:  F_{g,parallel} = (2.45 N) sin 50.0° = 1.88 N down the ramp

steps.say: b. The pull down the ramp grows and the normal force shrinks. A steeper ramp holds up less of the weight.
F_{g} is the same 2.45 N at both angles. Only how it splits changes.

questions.prompt: Lena is pushing her little brother up the driveway in a wagon. The driveway is steep, tilted 20.0° above the horizontal, and the wagon plus her brother come to 22.0 kg. She pushes with 60.0 N parallel to the driveway. Ignore friction.
parts: a.  Find the net force on the wagon along the driveway, with its direction.
b.  Is her push enough to keep the wagon from rolling back down?
questions.solution:
Down the driveway is positive. Fg,parallel = 22.0 × 9.8 × sin 20.0° = 73.7 N down the driveway. ∑F = 73.7 − 60.0 = 13.7 N down the driveway.
b. No. The forces are not balanced: the net force points down the driveway. It would take 73.7 N up the driveway to balance.
questions.finalAnswer: a. 13.7 N down the driveway. b. No; it would take 73.7 N.

steps.say: b. No. It would take 73.7 N up the driveway to balance.

questions.prompt: On an icy sledding hill tilted 15.0° above the horizontal, Dad holds the rope so the sled won't slide while his daughter climbs on. Sled and daughter have a mass of 32.0 kg, and the rope runs parallel to the hill. Treat the ice as frictionless. How hard does Dad have to pull to hold the sled still?
questions.solution: At rest, so ∑F along the hill = 0. T = Fg,parallel = 32.0 × 9.8 × sin 15.0° = 81.2 N up the hill.
questions.finalAnswer: 81.2 N up the hill, parallel to it

steps.say: The same pull would let the sled slide down at a constant speed. ∑F = 0 either way.

questions.prompt: Two movers roll a 65.0 kg refrigerator on a hand truck up the ramp into their truck. The ramp is tilted 18.0° above the horizontal, and they push parallel to it. Ignore friction.
parts: a.  What push moves the fridge up the ramp at a constant speed?
b.  What is the normal force from the ramp?
c.  If they push with 255 N instead, what is the net force on the fridge?
questions.solution:
Fg = 65.0 × 9.8 = 637 N.
a. Constant speed: ∑F = 0, so Fapp = 637 sin 18.0° = 197 N up the ramp.
b. FN = 637 cos 18.0° = 606 N perpendicular to the ramp.
c. Up the ramp positive: ∑F = 255 − 196.8 = 58 N up the ramp.
questions.finalAnswer: a. 197 N up the ramp. b. 606 N perpendicular to the ramp. c. 58 N up the ramp.

row: a.  constant speed:  ∑F = 0, so F_{app} = mg sin θ
c.  up the ramp = +:  ∑F = 255 N − 196.8 N

steps.say: Constant speed is ∑F = 0, the same as holding it still. A moving object does not need a net force.
